newsitem.title: USA: Textron, GEC get $1.5 bln Navy contract.
newsitem.headline: Textron, GEC get $1.5 bln Navy contract.

text.p: Textron Inc and Vickers Shipbuilding and Engineering said on Monday the companies received a U.S. Navy contract to produce a light field howitzer valued at $39.6 million, but the total program could exceed $1.5 billion.

The initial contract for the ultralightweight field howitzer has options for $110 million, the companies said in a joint statement. Vickers Shipbuilding and Engineering is a unit of General Electric Co Plc.
The howitzer contract is expected to secure 225 jobs in New Orleans at Textron Marine & Land Systems for the next decade, Textron and Vickers Shipbuilding said.
The Ultralightweight Field Howitzer will replace the 25-year old M-198 155mm towed howitzer currently used by the U.S. Marine Corps and the U.S. Army, the companies said.

This new weapon will provide close and deep fire support and interdiction fire as a direct support weapon for the Marine Corps, the companies said. The Army's Airborne, Air Assault and Light Forces will use the UFH as a general support weapon, the companies said.

Under the terms of the contract, there will be a three year funded engineering and manufacturing and development phase, during which Textron, as the prime contractor, will assure delivery and support of eight towed howitzers for testing, Textron and GEC's Vickers Shipbuilding said.

After that phase, it is expected that full-scale production will be initiated for more than 190 units, the companies said. The total United States Marine Corps and Army requirement is expected to exceed 1,300 light howitzers, the companies said.

Production of the guns that weigh less than 9,000 pounds will begin immediately and delivery of the first gun is set for September 1998 with the remaining seven due May 1999, Textron and GEC's Vickers Shipbuilding said.
Full production is expected in the year 2000, the companies said.
The Ultralight Field Howitzer offers greater ground mobility and improved reaction times compared to the 16,000 pound M198 Howitzer it will replace, the companies said.

In addition to filling U.S. requirements, this contract forms the basis for a cooperative program between the U.S. Government and the British Ministry of Defense, which has a requirement for a rapidly deployable howitzer, the companies said.
